findings.explanation: A large bidirectional traffic storm is saturating the links between cisco1, arista2 and hp1 toward router r1 on VLANs 10/20 (pc2<->r1 and srv1<->r1 flows each ~100k pps). This is orders of magnitude above the 3-second baseline seen elsewhere and is consistent with a broadcast/unknown-unicast storm or a forwarding loop on the r1 segment; the low-rate standby link arista1:4-arista2:4 being down should not cause this. Left unchecked it will drop legitimate traffic and exhaust switch/CPU resources.
findings.recommended_action: Trace the source of the ~100k pps on r1/pc2/srv1 (span or NetFlow), verify no L2 loop exists between cisco1, arista2 and hp1, enable storm-control/broadcast suppression on cisco1:1,3,4 and hp1:1,2, and check pc2/r1 for a misbehaving NIC or looped cable.
